core_obligations: Set up the cochain notation x = (x_{i_0 ... i_p}) together with the explicit formula for the differential d (proof lines 6988-6997).

Define the homotopy h on cochains of degree p+2 by splitting into the case where the distinguished index i occurs among i_0 to i_p, where h is zero, and the case where it does not, where h inserts i at its ordered position with the sign (-1)^j (proof lines 6997-7016).

Verify the contraction identity (dh + hd)(x) = -x on a fixed cochain of degree p+1, in Case I where i already occurs among the indices and in Case II where it does not, matching the signs of the two resulting sums (proof lines 7019-7061).
Conclude that the complex is homotopy equivalent to zero because it admits the contracting homotopy h (proof lines 7017-7018 and 7061-7062).

difficulty_reason: The statement is a vanishing statement for the extended alternating Cech complex of an arbitrary module: if one of the elements f_i is a unit then the complex is homotopy equivalent to zero (statement lines 6980-6986). Its proof is the longest completely written-out argument of this batch (proof lines 6988-7063): the author fixes cochain notation, writes down the differential explicitly, guesses an explicit homotopy h whose formula depends on whether the fixed index i already occurs in the multi-index, and verifies by a two-case computation that dh + hd is minus the identity. The non-routine part is precisely that computation: in the second case the signs of the two sums have to be matched term by term (proof lines 7036-7061), and the formula for h only makes sense because f_i being a unit lets the localisations with and without f_i be identified (proof lines 7009-7016). Nothing is left to the reader and no cited result is used.
